{
  "subtype": "focus_inference",
  "implied_focus": "Incident triage prioritization -- inferring which incidents (and why) warrant attention based on their nature, severity, and blast radius",
  "per_column": [
    {"name": "problem_domain", "supports_focus": true, "rationale": "Classifies the incident into a technical domain (database, email, vpn), a core facet of characterizing what an incident is about and where attention should go."},
    {"name": "severity_signal", "supports_focus": true, "rationale": "Encodes impact type (outage, access_degraded, infrastructure_failure) -- directly a prioritization/attention signal derived from the description."},
    {"name": "scope_context", "supports_focus": true, "rationale": "Captures blast radius (enterprise_system, building_wide, single_user), a key attention facet: broad-scope incidents warrant more attention."},
    {"name": "caller_recurrence", "supports_focus": false, "rationale": "Derived from caller_id metadata rather than the description's substance; only loosely tied to 'what's worth attention' and drifts toward a caller-analytics facet."},
    {"name": "technician_workload", "supports_focus": false, "rationale": "Describes assignee load, an operational/staffing facet orthogonal to what makes an incident description worth attention; introduces scatter."}
  ],
  "focus_coherence": 0.68,
  "structure_quality": 0.7,
  "focus_actionability": 0.8,
  "rationale": "The first three columns cohere tightly around a single inferable focus -- triaging incidents by what/how-bad/how-wide -- forming a genuine multi-facet analytical structure at useful granularity (domain x severity x scope), not a restatement or noise. This focus is clearly actionable: an analyst can prioritize enterprise-wide outages in the database/vpn domains. However, the last two columns (caller_recurrence, technician_workload) pivot away from the description content toward caller/staffing analytics, diluting the single-focus centring and pulling the set partway toward a grab-bag. Hence solid but not maximal coherence and structure."
}
